This is a one-to-one function because each x value results in a unique f(x) value.
For example, only when x = 2 will f(x) = 4. There is no chance that a different value for x will also cause f(x) to equal 4.
f (x) is the inverse function of f(x) since f (x) reverses the corresponding x and f(x) values.
Only one-to-one functions have inverse functions.
